prompt: Where does the planner put `transition:slide`, and why there?

choices.text: On the page's `<main>`, so every element inherits it
choices.why: Transitions are not inherited; each element that comes and goes carries its own.

choices.text: On the `<li>` in `List`, since `List` creates the rows
choices.why: Right. The transition goes on the element that is created and destroyed.

choices.text: On the row snippet in the page, since the page writes the content
choices.why: The snippet's content is the page's, but the `<li>` that comes and goes is `List`'s.

choices.text: In `vite.config.js`, where animations are switched on for a project
choices.why: A transition is an attribute on an element; there is nothing to switch on.

prompt: Right after `Previous week`, how many session rows did `look` print for Linear algebra?
Why does a screen reader still find the 19th's row for a moment after the week changed?
hint: When is a leaving element removed?

choices.text: It stays in the page until its outro ends
choices.why: Right, which is a reason to keep outros short.

choices.text: The browser caches the accessibility tree for one second
choices.why: The tree is current; the element is simply still there.

choices.text: `look` prints the page before the click, out of habit
choices.why: It printed the 13th too, which only exists after the click.

choices.text: The week has not changed yet; the button waits for the animation
choices.why: The week changed at once; the label already showed 12 October.

prompt: Moving to an empty week removed two rows with no animation. Why?
hint: Which block threw the rows away?

choices.text: Slides only play when rows are added, never when they leave
choices.why: Going back a week showed rows sliding out.

choices.text: The browser skips animations when a list becomes empty
choices.why: Nothing in the browser decides this; Svelte's local rule does.

choices.text: The `{#if}` took the `{#each}` with it
choices.why: Right: local transitions only play for their own block, and `|global` would make them play here too.

prompt: The modifier that makes a transition play even when an outer block is destroyed is written `transition:slide|___`.
Why does `ofCourse` use `toSorted` rather than `sort`?

choices.text: `sort` cannot compare date strings
choices.why: It can, with the same comparison function.

choices.text: It returns a copy, so the derived value does not reorder `sessions` itself
choices.why: Right: sorting state in place inside a derived value is a side effect.

choices.text: `animate:flip` only works with lists that were made by `toSorted`, never with arrays sorted in place
choices.why: `flip` needs a keyed each, not a particular way of sorting.

choices.text: `toSorted` is faster on short arrays
choices.why: Speed is not the reason given; leaving the state alone is.

prompt: Where may `animate:flip` be written?
hint: Svelte has to know which element moved.

choices.text: On any element with a transition
choices.why: A transition is not required, and not enough.

choices.text: On the `<ul>` around the list, so that all its children move together
choices.why: The `<ul>` does not move; its children do.

choices.text: On the direct child of a keyed `{#each}`
choices.why: Right. The key is how Svelte knows which element went where.

prompt: A moment after Enter, `look` showed the 21st already between the 19th and the 24th. What does that say about the animation?

choices.text: The animation had already finished; it lasts a few milliseconds
choices.why: It lasts much longer; the order was final from the start.

choices.text: The DOM changes at once; only where elements are drawn catches up
choices.why: Right. An animation never changes the order of the page.

choices.text: `look` sorts the tree by date before it prints it, whatever order the page is really in
choices.why: It prints the tree in page order.

prompt: Put the four steps of FLIP in order.
items: Apply the change and measure again
Draw each element back at its old place with a transform
trap: You cannot invert before you know both positions.

prompt: What is a `Tween` for?
hint: A transition is for an element.

choices.text: A value that travels to its new number
choices.why: Right. Elements get transitions; values get tweens.

choices.text: An element that enters the page from the side
choices.why: That is a transition such as `fly`.

choices.text: A list whose rows change order
choices.why: That is `animate:flip`.

choices.text: A store that saves a value between visits
choices.why: A tween remembers nothing between visits.

prompt: At `--wait 100`, what number did the sentence show?
The readings went 91, 106, 121, 150. What do they show about the tween's default easing?
hint: Compare the steps in the middle.

choices.text: It starts fast and slows into place
choices.why: That is `cubicOut`; the middle steps were equal.

choices.text: It is linear: a constant speed throughout
choices.why: Right: equal distance in equal time, about fifteen minutes every hundred milliseconds.

choices.text: It bounces past 150 and settles back
choices.why: That would be a `Spring`; no reading went past 150.

prompt: Why does every calculation read `doneMinutes` and only the sentence read `shownDone.current`?

choices.text: `shownDone.current` is not reactive outside markup
choices.why: Reading `current` is tracked anywhere.

choices.text: Tweens are only allowed in the markup
choices.why: The tween is created in the script.

choices.text: Mid-way, it is not a real number
choices.why: Right. A tween displays a value; it is never the value.

choices.text: `doneMinutes` would stop updating if the tween read it
choices.why: The tween does read it, through `Tween.of`, and it keeps updating.

prompt: In `flash`, `css` returns a background with alpha `(1 - t) * 0.6`. What does the student see during the intro?
hint: `t` runs from 0 to 1 across an intro.

choices.text: A highlight that grows stronger and stays
choices.why: At the end `t` is 1, so the alpha is 0.

choices.text: A highlight that starts strong and fades to nothing
choices.why: Right: `1 - t` goes from 1 to 0.

choices.text: The text itself fading in from transparent
choices.why: Only the background colour changes.

prompt: Why does `WeekTotal` wrap its paragraph in `{#key minutes}`?

choices.text: To stop the paragraph from updating twice, once for the total and once for the label beside it
choices.why: It updates once either way; the block is about creating it again.

choices.text: Because `in:` only works inside a `{#key}`
choices.why: `in:` works in any block; it plays when the element is created.

choices.text: A transition plays on creation, and the key creates the paragraph again on each change
choices.why: Right: lesson 8's `{#key}`, used to replay an intro.

prompt: Match each easing with how it feels.
hint: Look at the figure's three curves.

pairs.right: Fast at first, settling gently: something arriving
Gentle at first, abrupt at the end: something leaving
A constant speed, rarely right for movement

right_distractors: A bounce past the target before settling

prompt: What does returning `css` rather than changing styles from JavaScript on every frame gain?

choices.text: The browser plays it off the main thread, smooth while scripts are busy
choices.why: Right. Svelte turns the answers into keyframes once.

choices.text: It works in browsers with JavaScript turned off
choices.why: The transition is still started by Svelte's JavaScript.

choices.text: It makes the transition respect reduced motion by itself
choices.why: The next section shows it does not.

prompt: A stylesheet rule sets every `transition-duration` to zero for reduced motion. Why do the planner's slides still play?

choices.text: The rule is overridden by the component's scoped styles
choices.why: Scoping is not the issue; the transitions are not CSS transitions at all.

choices.text: They run on the Web Animations API, which that rule does not touch
choices.why: Right, so the component has to ask `prefersReducedMotion`.

choices.text: Chromium ignores the reduced motion setting
choices.why: `look --reduce-motion` set it, and the fixed version obeyed it.

prompt: With the setting on, what does a duration of 0 do to the planner?
hint: Look at the two captures with `--reduce-motion` after the change.

choices.text: It hides the rows and the numbers until the page is reloaded
choices.why: Everything is shown; it just arrives at once.

choices.text: It needs a second version of each component without animations
choices.why: The same components serve both settings.

choices.text: Outros end the moment they start, and the tween arrives the moment it is set
choices.why: Right: one row and 150 immediately.

prompt: The media query a browser matches for somebody who asked for less movement is `prefers-reduced-___: reduce`.
hint: The word this lesson is about.

prompt: Which response to reduced motion does the lesson warn against?

choices.text: Keeping a short fade while removing slides
choices.why: The lesson names that as a reasonable choice.

choices.text: Showing no sign that the session was added
choices.why: Right. Reduced means without travelling, not without change.

choices.text: Setting every duration to zero
choices.why: That is what the planner does, and everything still happens.

choices.text: Reading the setting through `prefersReducedMotion`
choices.why: That is the tool the lesson uses.

choices.text: The tween in `Planner`
